items.title: Bitcoin Sits Out Equity Fund Rush as Fed Hike Odds Reach 84%
items.summary:
Federal Reserve building as markets weigh the 10-year Treasury yield forecast. Photo by BeInCrypto

 

Global equity funds drew a record $266 billion in four weeks, per the Kobeissi Letter. Bitcoin (BTC) sat out the rush as Fed hike odds for December hit 84.4%.

That rush now meets a Fed that markets expect to tighten. Higher rates raise Treasury returns against non-yielding assets like Bitcoin, leaving BTC holders facing a second headwind.

## Who Is Capturing the Equity Fund Flows? [...] However, the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% on October 28 in a 10 to 2 vote. Officials Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike at that meeting.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin lagged the Nasdaq rebound on Friday. US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) saw $1.28 billion in net outflows from November 2 to 6, the analysis said. [...] Global equity funds gained $89 billion last week, with US funds supplying $32 billion of it. As a result, four-week inflows reached a record $266 billion, the post said.

## What Do 84% Fed Hike Odds Mean for Bitcoin?

The CME Group's FedWatch tool converts futures on the Fed's benchmark rate into probabilities. It shows an 84.4% chance of a quarter-point hike on December 9, with 0% assigned to a cut.

items.title: Miami-Dade property owners can now pay their property taxes with Bitcoin, tax collector says - CBS Miami
items.summary:
"Government must keep up with the times and the needs of the people we serve," Fernandez said in a statement. "Innovation is about making government more accessible, efficient, and convenient. By accepting Bitcoin as a payment option, we are giving property owners another way to pay their taxes, whether online or in person, while continuing to offer the traditional payment methods they already know and trust." [...] A third-party conversion system converts the digital currency into dollars at the time of payment. That conversion ensures the county receives the full dollar amount owed and integrates the transaction into the office's standard reconciliation and accounting reports without requiring county workers to maintain digital crypto wallets. [...] According to Fernandez, the new digital payment system will allow taxpayers to pay their tax bills through supported cryptocurrency exchange accounts or digital wallets, with every transaction automatically converted to U.S. dollars before the funds reach county accounts.

County officials emphasized that the Tax Collector's Office will not hold, invest in, or manage any cryptocurrency directly, thereby protecting public funds from the unpredictability of the crypto market.

items.title: Miami-Dade Tax Collector now accepts Bitcoin for property tax payments
items.summary:
Recommended Videos

“Government must keep up with the times and the needs of the people we serve,” Fernandez said. “Innovation is about making government more accessible, efficient, and convenient. By accepting Bitcoin as a payment option, we are giving property owners another way to pay their taxes, whether online or in person, while continuing to offer the traditional payment methods they already know and trust.”

### How it works [...] ### How it works

Property owners who choose to pay with Bitcoin can select the cryptocurrency option during the online checkout process or request it when paying in person. From there, users connect a supported cryptocurrency exchange account or digital wallet and authorize the payment.

The transaction is then automatically converted into U.S. dollars before the funds reach the Tax Collector’s Office — meaning the office never holds, invests in or manages cryptocurrency directly. [...] “Residents deserve a government that moves forward, not one that falls behind,” Fernandez said. “We are embracing new technology without compromising our responsibility to protect taxpayer dollars. Whether someone chooses to pay with Bitcoin or a traditional payment method, our office receives the full amount owed in U.S. dollars. This is about providing more choices while maintaining the financial accountability and transparency our residents expect.”
